subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Adapted and Lifelong Inclusive Activity Design
title: Correction and reflection: letting go of an activity without letting go of activity under transfer
focus: letting go of an activity without letting go of activity
essentialQuestion: How does an activity have to change to still be there at forty, or after an injury?
privacySafeScenario: Take one activity the learner values and produce three adapted versions of it — for reduced mobility, for very limited time, and for a mixed-age group — with the reasoning for each.
studentTask: Learner works letting go of an activity without letting go of activity by redesigning the learner’s own activity for age forty, for a changed capability, and for a mixed-age group at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of letting go of an activity without letting go of activity degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds letting go of an activity without letting go of activity by redesigning the learner’s own activity for age forty, for a changed capability, and for a mixed-age group, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: Adaptations may be written, diagrammed, described aloud, or trialed practically; practical trial is optional.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of letting go of an activity without letting go of activity yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Adaptations may be written, diagrammed, described aloud, or trialed practically; practical trial is optional.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where letting go of an activity without letting go of activity shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
